CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right big toe pain with redness

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports right great toe pain and erythema present intermittently for approximately 2 weeks, with significant worsening over the past week. Patient recalls being at a trade show convention where he was unable to walk the halls due to pain and had to remain standing. Pain is characterized as throbbing with occasional sharp, stabbing quality, particularly with movement or prolonged walking. Patient has modified his gait, walking on his heels to avoid bending the affected toe. Patient does not recall a specific injury. Patient became concerned when the toe became erythematous and warm to touch. Even light pressure to the toe is bothersome, including contact with bedding at night. Patient has taken ibuprofen 2 tablets daily without significant relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies stomach problems. Reports pain exacerbated by light pressure and at night.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 2 tablets daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works on his feet daily. Patient is an avid cyclist with over 800 miles of trail riding in the past year, wearing regular shoes on pedals. Patient typically wears flip-flops. Patient enjoys fishing.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right foot examined. Great toe noted to be erythematous. Range of motion testing of the first metatarsophalangeal joint reveals pain with plantarflexion at 10 degrees, with increased pain at 20 degrees plantarflexion. Dorsiflexion produces pain but less than plantarflexion. Medial-lateral manipulation of the joint produces pain with associated grinding sensation. Palpation between the first and second toes causes mild discomfort. Palpation of the lateral aspect of the great toe produces significant pain. Bone spur palpable on the dorsal surface of the first metatarsophalangeal joint.

RESULTS
X-ray of the foot demonstrates a large bone spur on the dorsal aspect of the first metatarsophalangeal joint with significant cartilage loss.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hallux rigidus with dorsal bone spur and cartilage loss of the first metatarsophalangeal joint.

Plan:
1. Orthotic shoe insert for conservative management.
2. Initiate meloxicam 1 tablet daily for anti-inflammatory effect. Counseled patient regarding potential gastrointestinal side effects including heartburn and epigastric pain, instructed to discontinue and contact office if these symptoms develop. Patient denies prior stomach problems.
3. Patient instructed to continue regular work and daily activities to assess treatment efficacy.
4. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to reassess response to treatment.
5. If inadequate response to conservative treatment, will consider more invasive options including corticosteroid injection or surgical intervention such as joint debridement or arthrodesis (joint fusion).
